description: Check a project's lockfile or pinned manifest against EchelonGraph's advisory corpus, one verdict per dependency. Pass files: 1 to 20 of filename and content, up to 5,000,000 characters in all; the filename, or format, gives the format. Read: requirements.txt (== and === pins only), go.mod (require, after replace and exclude), package-lock.json and npm-shrinkwrap.json (v1 to v3), Cargo.lock, Gemfile.lock, composer.lock, poetry.lock and gradle.lockfile. package.json, pyproject.toml, Pipfile, Gemfile, Cargo.toml, composer.json and build.gradle hold ranges and are refused, naming the lockfile to pass; go.sum is refused: it lists versions the build does not select. This server reads the files into purls and only the purls are sent to the API, in POST bodies of at most 200, never in a URL; filenames and file contents are not sent on. Run from npm, this server is on your machine; over the hosted endpoint (mcp.echelongraph.io) it is EchelonGraph's, and the files are the request body, accepted up to 6 MiB. data.results holds one row per distinct purl, with verdict (affected, not_affected, undetermined or not_assessed), not_assessed_reason, cve_ids and matched_via; each match carries kev_listed, epss_score and fixed_in or null with fixed_in_reason. not_affected is the only clean verdict. data.not_checked lists each entry not sent, with file, line and reason: version_unpinned (a range), version_unresolved, local_path, vcs_source or unsupported_line; not_checked entries are not clean. At most 2,000 distinct purls per call, within 50 seconds; data.not_sent_purls lists any not sent, unchecked and not clean. Past 30,000 characters of JSON, the first text block holds data cut to fit, and the note says what the cut leaves out and where to read it (TEXT CUT); data in the structured result always holds it whole. Cut, each row keeps index, purl, verdict, not_assessed_reason and cve_ids at least; not_checked keeps its first 20.

files.description: 1 to 20 files, up to 5,000,000 characters of content in all; read by this MCP server into purls, and only the purls are sent to the API; over the hosted endpoint (mcp.echelongraph.io) the files are the request body

content.description: the file's text, as it is on disk

filename.description: the file's name, e.g. package-lock.json or services/api/go.mod; it picks the format unless format is set

format.description: the format to read the file as, when its name does not say

name: scan_manifest

batch_size.description: The most purls one request carries (the API's cap per request).

batches.description: Requests the distinct purls make, at batch_size each.

batches_sent.description: Of those, the ones the API answered.

distinct_purls.description: Distinct purls to check: sent plus not_sent.

duplicates_removed.description: Purls read more than once (the same package and version in two places) and sent once.

entries_pinned.description: Entries pinned to one version across the files, duplicates included.

files_not_read.description: The ones refused or unreadable: nothing in them is checked, and none is clean.

not_assessed.description: Of those sent, the components with no verdict, as the answer counts them.

not_sent.description: Distinct purls not sent, listed in data.not_sent_purls: not checked, and not clean.

not_sent_reason.description: Why not_sent is above 0: time_budget (the call's 50 s budget ran out, before a batch or while one was unanswered, which is then cut off; or waiting out the API's Retry-After would pass it), rate_limited (a 429 without Retry-After, or a 429 after 10 waits), request_failed (a batch after the first failed; the note quotes how). null when every purl was sent.

partial.description: true when not every purl was sent (not_sent above 0) or any batch's summary.partial was true (its time budget ran out first); otherwise the answer's summary.partial.

rate_limit_waits.description: How many times the API answered 429 and the tool waited its Retry-After before sending the batch again.

coverage.description: What the answer covers; null where the answer says nothing about it.

manifest.description: Each file passed, in order, and how it was read. Filenames and contents are not sent to the API.

ecosystem.description: The OSV ecosystem of the purls read from it.

format.description: The format the file was read as: set by format, or read from the filename; null when it was not read.

not_checked.description: Entries not sent, listed in data.not_checked: not clean.

notes.description: How this file was read where that limits what its verdicts cover (a go.mod below go 1.17).

purls.description: Entries pinned to one version, read as purls (duplicates included).

read.description: false: the file was refused or could not be read, and nothing in it is checked (not clean).

refused.description: Why the file was not read, and the file to pass instead where there is one; null when it was read.

replaced.description: go.mod replace directives applied: the module required, and the module and version checked instead.

skipped.description: Entries that are not dependencies (a package-lock's root entry, the project itself).

not_checked.description: Each entry not sent to the API, with its file, line and reason: not checked, and not clean.

line.description: 1-based line; null in a JSON lockfile, whose entries spec names by key.

reason.description: version_unpinned: a range or wildcard, not one version; version_unresolved: no single registry version (none given, a branch, or an excluded go.mod version); local_path: a directory, file or workspace member; vcs_source: a VCS checkout; unsupported_line: a line or entry this tool does not read (another file named by -r or -c, a direct URL, another registry).

spec.description: What the file says for the entry: its line, or its lockfile key and version (at most 200 characters).

not_sent_purls.description: The distinct purls not sent (coverage.not_sent_reason says why): not checked, and not clean. Present only when some were not sent.

assessed.description: Whether the matcher produced a verdict for this component. false is never clean.

matched_package.description: The package name the advisories were looked up by (#2836): the purl's own name, or, for a deb or apk purl with an upstream qualifier, the source package it names, which is how Debian and Alpine file advisories.

matched_version_from.description: Upstream rows: upstream when the qualifier named a version (upstream=name@version) and it was used, purl when the purl's own version was.

matched_via.description: Which name matched_package is: purl_name (the purl's name), upstream (the purl's upstream qualifier) or coordinates (the component's package).

epss_score.description: The CVE's EPSS score (FIRST), as EchelonGraph's record holds it; null when it has none.

fixed_in.description: The fixed bound of the advisory interval that holds this component's version, always above it. null when that interval records no fix (it ends at last_affected, or has no end) or no interval holds the version, with fixed_in_reason saying which.

fixed_in_reason.description: Why fixed_in is null; absent when fixed_in is a version.

interval.description: The advisory interval that holds this component's version (fixed is exclusive, last_affected inclusive); absent when no interval holds it.

kev_listed.description: Whether the CVE is in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, as EchelonGraph's record holds it.

match_reason.description: Why the advisory applies, with the advisory interval the version falls inside: "[A, B)" names the fixed version B, "[A, B]" the last affected version B. On an upstream row it ends by naming the source package and the purl name.

not_assessed_reason.description: Why assessed is false: package_not_in_advisory_corpus, no_decidable_advisory, advisory_lookup_failed, candidate_window_truncated, time_budget, distro_release_unknown, purl_type_unsupported, version_missing or invalid_component.

purl_name.description: Upstream rows: the purl's own (binary) package name, not looked up.

verdict.description: affected (count > 0); not_affected (assessed, no match, nothing undetermined: the only clean verdict); undetermined (advisories name the package, at least one could not be decided, none matched: not clean); not_assessed (no verdict: not clean).

not_affected.description: Components with a decided, clean verdict.

not_assessed.description: Components with no verdict: not clean.

distro_release_unknown.description: deb, apk or rpm purls without a distro qualifier naming the release, which EchelonGraph does not guess.

time_budget.description: Components the batch's time budget ran out before: not clean; check them again.

not_assessed_by_reason.description: The not_assessed components, counted by not_assessed_reason.

partial.description: true when the time budget ran out before every component was looked up.

undetermined.description: Components whose advisories could not all be decided and none matched: not clean.

freshness.description: The producing radar's last completed check (last_run_at), where the API serves one.

measured_at.description: When the underlying observation was made, as the API states it; null when the answer does not say or holds no observation.

state.description: measured: a measurement of what was asked; an exposure count is measured only with measured_at and method. not_assessed: the answer holds no dated measurement of what was asked, so no count in it is presented as one; it can still relay a count, as what the source holds on record, undated, and its notes (and exposure_state, where the result carries it) say what each count is.

batch_size.description: The most purls one request carries (the API's cap per request).

batches.description: Requests the distinct purls make, at batch_size each.

batches_sent.description: Of those, the ones the API answered.

distinct_purls.description: Distinct purls to check: sent plus not_sent.

duplicates_removed.description: Purls read more than once (the same package and version in two places) and sent once.

entries_pinned.description: Entries pinned to one version across the files, duplicates included.

files_not_read.description: The ones refused or unreadable: nothing in them is checked, and none is clean.

not_assessed.description: Of those sent, the components with no verdict, as the answer counts them.

not_sent.description: Distinct purls not sent, listed in data.not_sent_purls: not checked, and not clean.

not_sent_reason.description: Why not_sent is above 0: time_budget (the call's 50 s budget ran out, before a batch or while one was unanswered, which is then cut off; or waiting out the API's Retry-After would pass it), rate_limited (a 429 without Retry-After, or a 429 after 10 waits), request_failed (a batch after the first failed; the note quotes how). null when every purl was sent.

partial.description: true when not every purl was sent (not_sent above 0) or any batch's summary.partial was true (its time budget ran out first); otherwise the answer's summary.partial.

rate_limit_waits.description: How many times the API answered 429 and the tool waited its Retry-After before sending the batch again.

kind.description: What failed: the request (network, timeout), the answer (http, not_json, not_object, unexpected_shape), the input, or this server.

message.description: The cause: the API's own message, or what went wrong.

path.description: The API path requested, when a request was made.

status.description: The HTTP status, when the API answered one.

state.description: failed: the lookup did not complete. invalid_input: the input was refused, so nothing was looked up. Neither is a finding.

title: Check a lockfile against the advisory corpus
